raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds the AMD Quark MXFP4 checkpoint, [`amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4), to the [Qwen3.8-Flash-Next recipe](https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) as an MI355X variant at TP2 and TP1. It turns on the MI355X work from #59575 that is merged and currently supported by the stock ROCm nightlies.

## Claims

- On MI355X the builder now selects the MXFP4 variant (`meta.default_variant: { mi355x: mxfp4 }`) and renders TP2 for plain TP. The guide also gives TP1, since the checkpoint (169.8 GiB) fits on one GPU.
- The variant's MI355X settings:
  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`;
  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` (#55686);
  - `AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1`;
  - `--gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl`.
- On the stock nightly, the rendered commands serve at the checkpoint card's accuracy: GSM8K 0.967 at TP2, 0.967 at TP1 and 0.965 at TEP8, against the card's 0.965.
- Speculative decoding becomes opt-in on MI355X, so the rendered MI355X commands don't include MTP; a page note for MI355X says why. Every other GPU renders exactly as before.
- The guide describes the MXFP4 flags, the TEP8/TP2/TP1 choice and the validation results in prose, without a launch command. A troubleshooting entry for the MXFP4 variant covers the engine ready timeout on slow TP2 cold starts.

## Validation

**Renderer.** `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes in [vllm-project/recipes](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes) at 05b4c57. At 609f86b, I rendered every hardware × variant × strategy combination with `resolveCommand` from main and from this branch:
- 234 renders are identical, including every NVIDIA GPU and the other AMD GPUs.
- On MI355X, FP8 and BF16 differ only by the dropped `--speculative-config`.
- MXFP4 is new.

**End to end on MI355X.** The rendered commands ran as rendered on `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-83c078d955cd6e0c63d3b12abe669c8de936a370` (vLLM 0.32.1rc1.dev361, AITER 0.1.26, FlyDSL 0.4.0). That means the Rust frontend (the recipe default), prefix caching on, empty kernel caches and the checkpoint in the local Hugging Face cache. Each server ran alone on otherwise idle GPUs. On this node each TP2 rank took 380–450 s to load its weights (TP1: 24 s), which puts a cold TP2 start past the 600 s default, so the runs set `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800`. The recipe leaves the timeout at its default, since load time depends on the node's storage, and covers it in a troubleshooting entry for the MXFP4 variant.

| config | cold startup | GSM8K | output tok/s, c1 / c8 / c32 | median TPOT (ms), c1 / c8 / c32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TP2 | 622 s | 0.967 | 159 / 801 / 1384 | 5.75 / 7.96 / 22.6 |
| TP1 | 271 s | 0.967 | 153 / 751 / 1282 | 6.02 / 8.77 / 24.6 |
| TEP8 | 251 s | 0.965 | — / 665 / 1831 | — / 8.34 / 17.1 |

Each cell is one run. TP1 was benchmarked twice, and the two runs agreed within 0.3%. The guide's chat prompt returned a complete answer with reasoning on TP1.

```bash
# GSM8K, as on the checkpoint card: chat completions with thinking off, 5-shot, all 1,319 questions
python3 tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' --max-tokens 2048 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32

# Throughput, random 8k/1k
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 --port 8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <c> --num-prompts <max(16, 4c)> --seed 0 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl
```

<details>
<summary>TP2 startup on one GPU pair of the test node</summary>

TP2 failed to start on HIP 0,1 of the test node in all 7 attempts, while it started in all 15 attempts on HIP 4,5 and 6,7. In every failure but one, rank 1 died during the last graph capture after the JIT kernel warmup (`Worker proc VllmWorker-1 died unexpectedly`), without a traceback. The exception, the first attempt, ran with the default 600 s timeout and hit it.

The latest attempts ran the same image and command on HIP 0,1 and HIP 4,5 at the same time: HIP 0,1 failed, and HIP 4,5 started and produced the TP2 row above. A Python bisect of df6603f0..83c078d9 on HIP 4,5 started at every step, including at 83c078d9 itself. The failure therefore belongs to that GPU pair, not to vLLM or this recipe. TP1 on HIP 0 and TEP8 across all eight GPUs started normally.
</details>

## Details

- **Speculative decoding** is out of scope for now. MTP doesn't load from the published MXFP4 checkpoint until [its config.json fix](https://huggingface.co/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4/discussions/1) is merged (details in #63124). The schema has no per-variant feature switch, and a single-mode `spec_decoding` limited to the other variants fails validation ("every checkpoint must retain at least one usable mode"). This PR therefore uses `hardware_opt_in_features: { mi355x: [spec_decoding] }`. That also turns MTP off by default for FP8 on MI355X, which still offers it as a toggle. A `notes[]` entry for MI355X explains this, and the FP8 MI355X guide section no longer passes `--speculative-config`.
- **TP size.** The variant sets `tp: { mi355x: 2 }`. TP2 matches the checkpoint card's serving command. TP1 is also possible, but since the builder keeps one TP size per variant and GPU, TP1 is only documented in the guide.
- **Strategy.** The recipe's `default_strategy` is `single_node_tep`, so the builder's MI355X default is TEP8. That works since #60816 made native AITER W4A4 MoE the default at TEP8, and it is validated above. DEP is also offered by the recipe's strategy list but wasn't tested with this variant.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ <https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/contributing>** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

Hi @mjkvaak-amd — we ran the MXFP4 variant on MI355X (2× and 4× GPUs) and can fill in part of the TODO table. All flags match the recipe as rendered (AITER, FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS, FlyDSL MoE sorting, `--gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl`, prefix caching, `qwen3_coder`/`qwen3` parsers), served from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (= `83c078d9`).

**Results:**

| config | startup | GSM8K (1319) | output tok/s c1 / c8 / c32 | median TPOT c1 / c8 / c32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 (recipe) | ~10 min | 0.956 | 131.5 / 823.3 / 1657.1 | 6.9 / 9.0 / 18.8 ms |
| TP4 (same flags) | ~12 min | 0.957 | 126.2 / 822.6 / 1844.2 | 7.2 / 9.2 / 16.3 ms |
| TP2 + QR INT8 | ~10 min | — | 152.0 / 920.5 / 2080.1 | 5.9 / 8.2 / 14.2 ms |
| TP2 + QR INT4 | ~10 min | — | 159.4 / 944.9 / 1816.3 | 5.8 / 8.0 / 17.3 ms |

lm_eval flexible-extract (250-question subset, greedy): TP2 no-QR 0.916, TP4 0.888, TP2 QR INT4 0.884.

QuickReduce runs were bare-metal (QuickReduce and the AITER custom all-reduce rely on `hipIpcGetMemHandle`, which fails inside Docker containers — both ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10 flavors — so the container baseline above uses `--disable-custom-all-reduce` + `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1`, which also disables QuickReduce as a side effect). The QuickReduce boot log confirms `['QUICK_REDUCE', 'AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` engaged.

> The YAML changes look right to me: `default_variant`, `supported_hardware`, `tp: { mi355x: 2 }` and the MI355X overrides. Turning MTP off through `hardware_opt_in_features` is also a reasonable workaround for the schema limit you describe. My comments are about the new guide section.

The guide repeats a command the builder already renders.** The recipes repo's [add-recipe skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/.agents/skills/add-recipe/SKILL.md) says: "The builder renders the command. Nothing that it can render belongs in the guide: no `vllm serve` launch commands, no environment blocks." Guide commands aren't generated or checked, so they drift. The `export …` plus `vllm serve …` block is the `single_node_tp` rendering of `variants.mxfp4.hardware_overrides.mi355x`, so it can go.
> 
> **2. "TP2 is the default the command builder renders" is not what the page renders.** The recipe's `default_strategy` is `single_node_tep`. The preview's JSON API ([`/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4.json`](https://vllm-recipes-git-preview-vllm-pr-63332-inferact-inc.vercel.app/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4.json)) gives this `recommended_command`:
> 
> ```
> strategy: single_node_tep
> vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 ... --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 ...
> ```
> 
> TP2 only appears when the reader picks the TP strategy. The PR description's Details section says the same ("the builder's MI355X default is TEP8"), so the guide contradicts it. This is the drift from point 1.
> 
> **3. The most useful facts are only in the PR description.**
> 
> * **MTP is off on MI355X**, because the MXFP4 checkpoint's MTP doesn't load until the HF `config.json` fix lands. As a side effect, FP8 and BF16 on MI355X no longer render MTP by default.
>   
>   * Readers of the page won't know why.
>   * The existing "FP8 configuration on a 4x MI355X GPU" section still passes `--speculative-config`, so it no longer matches the default command.
> * **A cold TP2 start can exceed the 600 s ready timeout**, and readers will hit it.
> * **The validation is not in the recipe**: the tested image `nightly-83c078d955cd…`, GSM8K 0.967/0.967/0.965 at TP2/TP1/TEP8, and the throughput numbers.
> 
> **4. Time-relative wording.** "the MI355X work merged so far under #59575" will go stale. The tested nightly image or commit says the same thing and stays true.
> 
> **Suggested layout**
> 
> Content	Where
> The env and `--gdn-prefill-backend` command block	remove; the variant's `hardware_overrides` render it
> Checkpoint link and what each flag does	guide, as prose
> The default is TEP8 and TP2 is offered. TP1 also works because the checkpoint fits on one GPU; the builder holds one TP size per variant and GPU, so TP1 is prose	guide, as prose
> Tested image, GSM8K, a short throughput table	guide, naming the variant and hardware
> "MTP is off by default on MI355X: the MXFP4 checkpoint can't load it yet; FP8 can still turn it on"	`notes[]` with `when: { hardware: [mi355x] }`
> TP2 cold start exceeds the ready timeout; set `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800`	`troubleshooting[]` with the error text as `title` and `when: { variants: [mxfp4] }`
> `--speculative-config` in the existing FP8 MI355X section	drop it, or say MTP is now opt-in there. That section already broke the no-commands rule, but this PR changes its MTP default
> `notes[]` and `troubleshooting[]` are described in [SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/SCHEMA.md). Both show on the page only for matching selections.

Thanks for the review! 🙏 Fixes applied in 8ad8656. 
* The MXFP4 command block is gone, and the flags are described in prose. 
* The guide now says TEP8 is the default and TP2 comes from the TP strategy, with TP1 in prose.

+  ### MXFP4 on MI355X
+
+  On MI355X, the MXFP4 variant serves AMD's

+  - `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`, which fuses the shared

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

The YAML changes look right to me: `default_variant`, `supported_hardware`, `tp: { mi355x: 2 }` and the MI355X overrides. Turning MTP off through `hardware_opt_in_features` is also a reasonable workaround for the schema limit you describe. My comments are about the new guide section.

**1. The guide repeats a command the builder already renders.**
The recipes repo's [add-recipe skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/.agents/skills/add-recipe/SKILL.md) says: "The builder renders the command. Nothing that it can render belongs in the guide: no `vllm serve` launch commands, no environment blocks." Guide commands aren't generated or checked, so they drift. The `export …` plus `vllm serve …` block is the `single_node_tp` rendering of `variants.mxfp4.hardware_overrides.mi355x`, so it can go.

**2. "TP2 is the default the command builder renders" is not what the page renders.**
The recipe's `default_strategy` is `single_node_tep`. The preview's JSON API ([`/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4.json`](https://vllm-recipes-git-preview-vllm-pr-63332-inferact-inc.vercel.app/amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4.json)) gives this `recommended_command`:

```
strategy: single_node_tep
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4 ... --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 ...
```

TP2 only appears when the reader picks the TP strategy. The PR description's Details section says the same ("the builder's MI355X default is TEP8"), so the guide contradicts it. This is the drift from point 1.

**3. The most useful facts are only in the PR description.**
- **MTP is off on MI355X**, because the MXFP4 checkpoint's MTP doesn't load until the HF `config.json` fix lands. As a side effect, FP8 and BF16 on MI355X no longer render MTP by default.
  - Readers of the page won't know why.
  - The existing "FP8 configuration on a 4x MI355X GPU" section still passes `--speculative-config`, so it no longer matches the default command.
- **A cold TP2 start can exceed the 600 s ready timeout**, and readers will hit it.
- **The validation is not in the recipe**: the tested image `nightly-83c078d955cd…`, GSM8K 0.967/0.967/0.965 at TP2/TP1/TEP8, and the throughput numbers.

**4. Time-relative wording.**
"the MI355X work merged so far under #59575" will go stale. The tested nightly image or commit says the same thing and stays true.

**Suggested layout**

| Content | Where |
|---|---|
| The env and `--gdn-prefill-backend` command block | remove; the variant's `hardware_overrides` render it |
| Checkpoint link and what each flag does | guide, as prose |
| The default is TEP8 and TP2 is offered. TP1 also works because the checkpoint fits on one GPU; the builder holds one TP size per variant and GPU, so TP1 is prose | guide, as prose |
| Tested image, GSM8K, a short throughput table | guide, naming the variant and hardware |
| "MTP is off by default on MI355X: the MXFP4 checkpoint can't load it yet; FP8 can still turn it on" | `notes[]` with `when: { hardware: [mi355x] }` |
| TP2 cold start exceeds the ready timeout; set `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=1800` | `troubleshooting[]` with the error text as `title` and `when: { variants: [mxfp4] }` |
| `--speculative-config` in the existing FP8 MI355X section | drop it, or say MTP is now opt-in there. That section already broke the no-commands rule, but this PR changes its MTP default |

`notes[]` and `troubleshooting[]` are described in [SCHEMA.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/SCHEMA.md). Both show on the page only for matching selections.
